adverse_media.summary: Wirecard reported €1.9bn in missing cash and €3.2bn in debt and filed for insolvency for over-indebtedness. Munich police had searched its headquarters on 2020-06-05. It was a DAX member until August 2020.

Munich criminal trial of ex-CEO Markus Braun, Oliver Bellenhaus and the former chief accountant for invented revenues booked through third-party partners in Dubai, Singapore and the Philippines (charged March 2022). On 2026-09-14 the court called Braun's victim theory 'speculation' and warned of confiscation (about €39m for Braun). Closing arguments were scheduled for 2026-10-19.
adverse_media.status: Pending, no verdict found as of 2026-10-30; Braun in pretrial detention since July 2020

adverse_media.summary: Munich Regional Court ordered Braun and two other former executives to pay about €140m in damages to the insolvency administrator over unrepaid loans to an Asian business partner.
BaFin fined Wirecard AG about €1.5m (€1.52m) for late publication of its 2018 half-year financial report and for not promptly disclosing where it could be accessed.
Singapore's MAS directed Wirecard's Singapore branch to stop payment services and return customer funds. In June 2020 the UK FCA froze Wirecard Card Solutions Ltd.

Singapore courts sentenced R Shanmugaratnam to 10 years and James Henry O'Sullivan to 6.5 years for falsifying accounts tied to the Wirecard fraud. Earlier, in June 2023, James Wardhana got 21 months and Chai Ai Lim 10 months.

adverse_media.category: Fugitive executive / alleged money laundering and Russian intelligence links
adverse_media.summary: Ex-COO Jan Marsalek is a fugitive on the BKA wanted list with an INTERPOL Red Notice. Media say he is in Moscow, call him a Russian intelligence handler (named in a UK espionage charging document) and, citing the FT in November 2025, tie him to a money-laundering network involving sanctioned oligarchs.

Wirecard sued the Financial Times. Munich prosecutors opened an investigation into FT journalist Dan McCrum (February 2019). US prosecutors and the FBI reportedly looked into hacking-for-hire allegations against Wirecard critics.
adverse_media.status: Historical; outcome of the hacking probe not confirmed

output.risk_rationale: Wirecard AG (HRB 169227, Amtsgericht München, LEI 529900A8LX4KL0YUTH71, now lapsed) has been in court insolvency since 2020-08-25 under administrator Michael Jaffé, after one of Europe's largest accounting frauds (€1.9bn of cash that did not exist). Its former CEO Markus Braun (Austrian) is still on criminal trial in Munich: closing arguments were set for October 2026 and no verdict was found as of 2026-10-30. Its former COO Jan Marsalek is an internationally wanted fugitive reportedly working for Russian intelligence and alleged in the media to be tied to money laundering for sanctioned parties. Related accounting-fraud convictions have followed in Singapore (2023 and January 2026), there is a €140m civil damages judgment against ex-executives that is not final, and BaFin fined the company in 2019. No sanctions matches were found for the entity, Marsalek or Braun, and no PEPs were found. The company is shut down and has no beneficial owner or PSC on record. The fraud, the ongoing criminal and insolvency proceedings and the links to a Russia-linked fugitive make any relationship other than dealing with the insolvency estate high risk. The registered address differs between sources: Humboldtstraße 8 (Implisense, 2025) versus Einsteinring 35 (GLEIF, 2020). The register-derived board listing (Freis, Steidl) may be out of date, since the administrator holds control. One namesake was excluded: Rafał Marszałek, a Polish person who came up in the Marsalek search.
